----Respondents
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vijay Kumar Gaur
 Mr. Chandan Singh Jodha
For Respondent(s) : Ms. Sonu Manawat, Pp
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Arun Monga
Order 10/10/2024
1.

Petitioner is before this Court seeking quashing of an FIR No.485/2023 dated 18.07.2023,
registered at Police Station Pilibanga, District Hanumangarh, for the alleged offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC.
2.
3. The petitioner allegedly offered to secure a job abroad for the complainant's son through his brother, Badal Singh, in exchange for Rs. 8,50,000.
However, after payment, the complainant received forged documents, including an appointment letter, and was unable to join the job.
Petitioner, however, asserts that FIR has been registered on the basis of false allegations leveled against him.
The same thus deserves to be quashed.

4. Having heard the contentions and upon perusal of case file and the FIR, I am of the view that it would not be appropriate to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction vested under Section 482 of [2024:RJ-JD:41673] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-5802/2023] Cr.P.C. (Now Section 528 of BNSS) and quash the FIR summarily on the basis of self serving affidavit of petitioners/accused.

sentences.text: Whether or not the allegations are false is a matter of investigation, and it is not for this Court at this preliminary stage to adjudicate on the same.

6. However, it is expected of the Investigating Officer to strictly follow the guidelines rendered by Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Anr 1 and proceed further in accordance with the law.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Anr 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Meanwhile, petitioner is directed to join the investigation.

If during the investigation, in case any incriminating material of such nature is found against the petitioner, which prima facie is suggestive of any cognizable offence committed by him, warranting his arrest, then a fresh notice under Section 35 of BNSS shall be given to him so as to enable him to seek legal remedy in accordance with the law.
8. Conversely, it is made clear that in case there is no incriminating material found against the petitioner, appropriate report be filed before the competent court expeditiously.
9. The instant petition is accordingly disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

(ARUN MONGA),J 59-DhananjayS/-
